messages:
ria: heads-up: seeing unexplained tail latency spikes on private-vpc cluster A after the midnight rollout. p95 jumped from 120ms -> 980ms around 00:12 UTC.
ria: graph: https://dash.redwood/internal/d/serving/cluster-a-latency?from=now-2h&to=now
dan: noticed similar on my builds, throughput dropped ~30% too. any correlation with batching changes?
samir: I rolled the kernel selection tweak yesterday (kernel-selector v1.3.1) and also enabled the new batching heuristic that favors larger batch windows under low-rps.
samir: my quick profiler shows a lot more sched_preempt and context_switches on NODES with egress heavy traffic. Flame: https://perf.redwood/tmp/2140000000-flame.svg
lucy: infra-oncall, can you check eBPF firewall logs? we added a rule for DNAT -> static ports last week.
infra-oncall: ops-bot reports many DROP->REINJECT events in eBPF chain from 00:10-00:20, looks like fragmentation handling path triggered. logs: `ebpf/fw: frag_reasm_timeout=120s count=312`
ben: that frag_reasm_timeout suggests packets hitting MTU fragmentation + eBPF reassembly. could be the NAT path doing hairpin + reassembly and delaying large requests.
dan: KV cache misses spiked at the same time for large prefix keys. correlated with partial token fetches -> more batching latency.
ria: paste of relevant traces: ```
[00:11:02] req_id=abcd kernel_selector=cpu_affined batch_id=402 step=kv_lookup hit=false
[00:11:02] req_id=abcd nat_snat=allocated:4096 port=60000 frag=1/3
[00:11:03] ebpf: drop->queue reassembly pending req_id=abcd
[00:11:04] batcher: waiting_for_fragments batch=402 timeout=200ms
[00:11:12] batcher: timeout -> flush batch=402 latency=980ms
```
samir: interesting: kernel-selector pinned inference worker to isolated cpu set to reduce jitter, but pinned thread handles reassembly syscalls which block and cause long syscalls and context switches. scheduling skew + eBPF queueing = big delay.
lucy: we also pushed a firewall tweak that clamps MSS on the egress path for container networking last week. maybe mismatch between MSS clamp and actual path MTU -> causes fragmentation.
ben: quick check: iptables/MSS clamp log shows `clamp_mss_to_pmtu` active on the bridge and MTU on host is 9000 but customer peering link MTU is 1500. so packets >1500 are fragmented and reassembly happens at eBPF.
infra-oncall: ops-bot ran a mitigation: temporary disable DNAT hairpin rule and revert kernel-selector affinity on two affected nodes at 00:25 UTC.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: reverted kernel-selector config `v1.3.1` -> `v1.3.0` on nodes [a3,a7], disabled DNAT-hairpin rule id=fw-234. Triggered rollback runbook step 2.
ria: after that latency dropped back to ~140ms by 00:32. throughput recovered.
dan: long-term fixes to consider: (1) make batching wait tolerant to reassembly delays by prioritizing ready shards, (2) avoid pinning reassembly-handling threads to inference cpus, (3) add MTU detection and automatic MSS clamp alignment on peering links, (4) add eBPF metrics for frag_reasm queue length.
samir: agree. I'll open a PR to change kernel-selector so it avoids assigning reassembly-intensive syscalls to inference cpus and to add a small backoff to the large-batch heuristic if frag_reasm_rate > threshold.
lucy: I'll file infra ticket to add MTU check during private-VPC onboarding and auto-adjust clamp flags.
ben: also recommend adding a KV cache metric to surface partial-fetch rate — that was the smoking gun.
ria: thanks all. created incident doc: https://docs.redwood/internal/incidents/2140000000-ebpf-frag-batch-lag and assigning follow-ups to samir/lucy/ben.
infra-oncall: marking as resolved for now, will monitor next 24h. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: note: postmortem reminder scheduled in 48h.
